changes: This is the Euskal Oiloa (Gallina Vasca). Purpose dual-purpose to dual (allowed value). Temperament changed from a list (friendly, hardy, good forager) to friendly; hardy and good forager are not temperament. Origin France/Spain to Spain: Wikipedia gives Spain as the country of origin and the breed standard is Spanish; Star Milling's France/Spain kept as a conflict alternative. Added hen 2.5 kg and rooster 3.6 kg from Wikipedia, with Star Milling's 9 lb (4.1 kg) rooster as an alternative. Confirmed 200 to 220 brown eggs a year (Wikipedia 209 to 220) and large size (Wikipedia about 60 g).

summary.value: The Basque hen, called Euskal Oiloa in the Basque language, is the old farmyard chicken of the Basque Country, the region that straddles northern Spain and southwestern France. It is a sturdy dual purpose bird that gave rural families both meat and eggs, and Spain began a formal breeding program for it in 1975. It has yellow legs and skin, red earlobes and a bright red single comb. Five color forms exist: black, red, a red brown naked neck, golden cuckoo and a white bird with a black tail. Cocks weigh about 8 to 9 pounds and hens about 5.5 pounds. Hens lay roughly 200 to 220 large brown eggs a year. The birds are friendly, like being around people and handle well. They are tough and forage well, which suits homesteads and free range flocks.
